subject: Using commandArgs() to run multiple lines at a time

messages.author: 1b13ff6a69693e4b
messages.subject: Using commandArgs() to run multiple lines at a time
parts:
Hi all,

I am trying to run these lines in different sessions to make a better use of memory. Because my files are so big, I need to partition my data frame all_df_0624_1201 in different chunks:

test_pred_all1 <- predict(svm_05082018_Radial_Landsatlike, newdata = all_df_0624_1201[i[1:1000000],])
test_pred_all2 <- predict(svm_05082018_Radial_Landsatlike, newdata = all_df_0624_1201[i[1000001:2000000],])
and so on...

So I am trying to use arguments from the command line (thanks Alex for the idea!)
If I run in the command line: Rscript --vanilla myscript.R 8
I would expect my script to run the eighth line:
test_pred_all8 <- predict(svm_05082018_Radial_Landsatlike, newdata = all_df_0624_1201[i[7000001:8000000],])

So, in my script, I am working on this function: 

i <- which(!is.na(all_df_0624_1201$NDVI_0624))

arg<-commandArgs()
chunk<-arg[1]
fun(chunk){
  end<-chunk*1000000
  start<-end-1000000-1
  return(start,end)
  test_pred_all8 <- predict(svm_05082018_Radial_Landsatlike, newdata = all_df_0624_1201[i[start:end],])
  saveRDS(test_pred_all8, file='C:/mypath/test_pred_all8.rds')
  }

What I don't understand is how to use chunk to create the variable test_pred_allchunk, and then the same thing to save them. How do I go from chunk to test_pred_all1, test_pred_all2, etc so every time I change the argument in the command line it saves a file with that number? 

Thanks in advance and happy Saturday!
Ana

Hi Ana

I am not sure I fully understand your issue, but is it that you want to adjust at every call the name test_pred_all_1, etc? Given that you use saveRDS, this is not really necessary: just doing readRDS() you will be able to assign a new name (unlike the behaviour of save/load where you indeed need to know ex-ante the name of the object. So I think all you need is to do adapt with paste() the output path:
res <- predict(svm_05082018_Radial_Landsatlike, newdata = all_df_0624_1201[i[start:end],])
 saveRDS(res, file=paste('C:/mypath/test_pred_all", chunk, ".rds'))

See below  minimum reproducible code. Note further that:
-the commandArg will likely be character, so make sure yo use as.numeric() where needed.
- you return(new, end) looks suspicious: you can only return a single object, possibly a list though
-I don;t think you necessarily need a function(chunk) in your code?

#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
arg <- commandArgs(trailingOnly=TRUE)
chunk<-arg[1]
print(chunk)

set.seed(123)
x <- rnorm(1:100)


res <- x[as.numeric(chunk)]
saveRDS(res, file = paste("result_", chunk, '.rds', sep=""))

messages.author: dec62abc2768b2b0
messages.subject: Re: [geospatial] Using commandArgs() to run multiple lines at a time
parts:
Ana,

You may just need to set the output file name for each chunk. 

You may consider additional measures to make the code more memory-safe. E.g. there is no need to find the all rows with NA for each chunk ( i <- which(!is.na(all_df_0624_1201$NDVI_0624)) ). You can find the rows with NA within each chunk, predict the cases without NA and keep the predicted values as NA for input with NA. In this way you will have equal number of rows between input and predictions, which will make it lot easier to create the raster of prediction (assuming that is your final goal). Your final myscript.R should look like:

arg<-commandArgs()
chunk<-arg[1]
fun(chunk){
  end<-chunk*1000000
  start<-end-1000000-1

indf <-  all_df_0624_1201[start:end,] 
  i <-   which(!is.na(indf$NDVI_0624))
  # now create an empty vector to store the results 
  prediction <- rep(NA, nrow(indf)) 
  prediction[i] <- predict(svm_05082018_Radial_Landsatlike, newdata = indf[i,])
  outfile <- paste0(' C:/mypath/ ','test_pred_all',chuck,'.rds') # set the output name for each chunk
  saveRDS( prediction, file = outfile)
  return(c(start,end, nrow(indf), length(prediction))
  } 

Please note that I have not tested running the above code as Rscript (only tested parts with dummy data). You may need to adapt it for your data.

Thanks,
-Ani

It looks like the code is declaring a function, but not assigning it to a variable or calling it (i.e., not doing anything with it).  Try something like this:

    [the function declaration as you have it]
}

process_chunk(chunk)

print(“Done”)

Also, is all_df_0624_1201 (line 23) loaded when you load the model on line 16?  Otherwise it doesn’t seem to be loaded anywhere, and the function will throw an error when you call it.  Maybe this should just be the df that you load on line 13?

Ana,

Sorry, I didn't test the previous function from the terminal. The function was defined but it wasn't set to execute. Please see the attached function that works for me in the terminal. You need the change the variables inside based on your input names.

I have some other questions about your data that is more remote sensing related. Why do you have 'NaN' in the vegetation indices? NaN means 0/0 and not same as NA. Almost all the time these indices are defined such that they return values within specific range for 'real' surface reflectance of the bands. Having 0 in all bands is unlikely unless the specific pixel is masked. You should recheck your calculation (mostly the preprocessing and how you are storing the output, integer vs float).

Thanks,
-Ani

On Sat, Jul 21, 2018 at 5:39 PM, Aniruddha Ghosh <anig...@ucdavis.edu> wrote:

Ana,

You may just need to set the output file name for each chunk. 

You may consider additional measures to make the code more memory-safe. E.g. there is no need to find the all rows with NA for each chunk ( i <- which(!is.na(all_df_0624_1201$NDVI_0624)) ). You can find the rows with NA within each chunk, predict the cases without NA and keep the predicted values as NA for input with NA. In this way you will have equal number of rows between input and predictions, which will make it lot easier to create the raster of prediction (assuming that is your final goal). Your final myscript.R should look like:

arg<-commandArgs()
chunk<-arg[1]
fun(chunk){
  end<-chunk*1000000
  start<-end-1000000-1
  indf <-  all_df_0624_1201[start:end,] 
  i <-   which(!is.na(indf$NDVI_0624))
  # now create an empty vector to store the results 
  prediction <- rep(NA, nrow(indf)) 
  prediction[i] <- predict(svm_05082018_Radial_Landsatlike, newdata = indf[i,])
  outfile <- paste0(' C:/mypath/ ','test_pred_all',chuck,'.rds') # set the output name for each chunk
  saveRDS( prediction, file = outfile)
  return(c(start,end, nrow(indf), length(prediction))
  } 

Please note that I have not tested running the above code as Rscript (only tested parts with dummy data). You may need to adapt it for your data.

Thanks,
-Ani

Sorry, I didn't test the previous function from the terminal. The function was defined but it wasn't set to execute. Please see the attached function that works for me in the terminal. You need the change the variables inside based on your input names.

I have some other questions about your data that is more remote sensing related. Why do you have 'NaN' in the vegetation indices? NaN means 0/0 and not same as NA. Almost all the time these indices are defined such that they return values within specific range for 'real' surface reflectance of the bands. Having 0 in all bands is unlikely unless the specific pixel is masked. You should recheck your calculation (mostly the preprocessing and how you are storing the output, integer vs float).
